items.title: Maude Johnson Interview, 1959-01-06
items.q: he went and seen the school board. For us. D-Loyd Porter. And he was talking to him about putting up a band

ctx.x: D-A-U-T-R-I-V-E. I don't know if you can understand.

And so I think when Louis Armstrong came by, he was in the rice field then. He had quit there and he went to the rice field then. Yeah, I think he must have been there. And after that, well, you started writing to him. Bill Russell started writing to him and everything. That's where he got together and he got his teeth. And then after that, he went and seen the school board. For us. D-Loyd Porter. And he was talking to him about putting up a band, a little school band, teaching school children. So then he had two…
Yes, and I still had it in 1942 when Gene Williams came down.
